findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

Several employees were observed to don gloves without prior hand washing. Education was conducted to correct the situation and the PICs were instructed to ensure that all staff are washing their hands at all times that it is required.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

On arrival the ice scoop for the kitchen fountain drink machine was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This would allow for bare hand contact of the Ready-To-Eat food (ice) when it is acquired for drinks. The PIC was shown and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that all utensils are stored so that the foods they are used for are protected from contamination from bare hand contact.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen was without paper towels or another approved hand drying system. The PIC was shown and replaced the paper towels to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sanitizer bucket in the bar area was observed with a concentration of approximately 10 ppm CL during the inspection. The PIC was shown and asked when the bucket was made. They stated approximately 2:00 (45 minutes prior to observation). The bucket was brought into compliance at 200 ppm CL to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers in the facility are maintained at effective concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Numerous TCS foods in the walk in cooler were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-51F. The PIC was shown and discarded the items to correct the immediate violation. Items discarded during this inspection include: 1) multiple buckets of salsa, 2) two half pans of chicken breasts, 3) three full pans of beef strips, 4) one pan of ground beef, 5) half of a full pan of sliced tomatoes, 6) a half pan of shrimp, 7) one, five gallon bucket of chopped lettuce, 8) 1.5 gallons of milk, 9) six half pans of queso, 10) one case of whipped topping, 11) one carton of heavy whipping cream, 12) two pans of marinated chicken, 13) one mostly consumed pan of pork, 14) one pan of Beria beef and 15) one case of American cheese. The cooler itself is being placed onto the line item #33 violation for follow-up. The facility was instructed not to use this cooler until effective cold holding temperatures could be maintained.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The walk in cooler for this facility was observed with ambient air temperatures of approximately 50F-51F. The TCS foods were discarded (refer to line item #22). This violation is for the cooler not functioning correctly. Another manager from another facility arrived and helped translate, while also instructing them to leave the walk in freezer door open to help in the short term. The PIC was instructed to have the walk in cooler repaired and functioning correctly prior to the scheduled follow up on 9/14/26.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A moist cloth was observed on top of the counter in the back prep area of the facility. This rag should be stored between uses in the relevant bucket of sanitizer to prevent pathogenic replication from taking place. The PIC was consulted and had the rag moved to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple knives were observed on the left most knife rack in the back prep area with brown lines on the blades. Investigation showed that the lines were from the magnetic rack that the knives were attached to. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The knives and rack were cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored in such a way as to be maintained clean prior to use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

A thick accumulation of frost and ice was observed in the walk in freezer on the shelves and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation moving forward. This issue may be resolved when the planned door replacement takes place, however it should be managed at all times regardless.  Ensure that all food areas are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Numerous flies are still observed throughout the facility, specifically by the hand sink and the mop sink next to the ice machine. Fly strips were suggested by the PIC and an enzymatic cleaner was suggested by the inspector for the drains. The PIC is instructed to contact their pest control agency for maintenance and to reduce/remove the pests. A follow up is being set for one month out to allow time for the chemicals likely needed to take effect.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection a CFPM was not available in the facility. The PIC is instructed to have a CFPM available at all times that the facility is in operation.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

The side door to the facility was observed to have a gap along the bottom seam sufficient to allow visible sunlight through. This indicates a gap sufficient for pest entrance into the facility. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Approximately 10 flies were observed throughout the facility, specifically by the hand sink, by the mop sink and in the storage room by the walk in cooler. The PIC is instructed to contact their pest control agency for maintenance and to reduce/remove the pests. A follow up is being set for one month out to allow time for the chemicals likely needed to take effect.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A moist cloth was observed on top of the container of dry beans in the back of the facility. It appears to be a hold over from the most recent cleaning took place for the nearby counter. This rag should be stored between uses in the relevant bucket of sanitizer to prevent pathogenic replication from taking place. The PIC was consulted and had the rag moved to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

A thick accumulation of frost and ice is observed in the walk in freezer on the shelves and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation moving forward. This issue may be resolved when the planned door replacement takes place, however it should be managed at all times regardless.  Ensure that all food areas are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An employee drink was observed stored in a container including sauces for consumers and other foods. The cook was shown and removed the item to correct. Ensure that all personal foods are stored separately from those intended for consumers in the facility.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection a CFPM was not available in the facility. The PIC is instructed to have a CFPM available at all times that the facility is in operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

The only hand sink in the bar area was observed with a pitcher in it as well as a pair of blenders in front of it preventing access and use. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain the hand sinks in the facility accessible at all times. The items were moved to correct.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The faucet to the triple sink had a plastic bag wrapped around it to prevent a leak from spraying out. This is not an approved method to repair plumbing. The PIC was instructed to have a plumber repair the faucet prior to the scheduled follow-up. The follow up was pushed back from the usual three days because of the weekend and holiday.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code.

In the walk in freezer, stacks of food in boxes are observed with the bottom boxes on the floor. These bottom boxes are saturated in ice and the dyes from the boxes appear to have soaked into the observable ice coating them. This leads to the conclusion that the food inside of these containers has been contaminated and should not be used. The PIC was notified and discarded the bottom containers of food to correct the immediate violation. The remaining boxes were then placed on milk cartons to correct the future concerns of this situation (refer to line item #39 for write up). Ensure that all foods are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Two stacks of boxes containing food are observed with the bottom boxes stored on the floor of the walk in freezer. The PIC was shown and placed the stacks on top of crates to correct. The bottom boxes were discarded (refer to line item #15 for write up). Ensure that all foods are stored at least six inches above the floor at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

A thick accumulation of frost and ice is observed in the walk in freezer on the shelves and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation moving forward. This issue may be resolved when the planned door replacement takes place, however it should be managed at all times regardless.  Ensure that all food areas are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers (CFPM) employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

The only allergen certificate currently available at the facility is held by an employee without a CFPM. None of the available CFPMs have an allergen training certificate. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all CFPMs at the facility have completed allergen training prior to the next routine inspection and that the certificates are maintained at the facility moving forward. Ensure that all CFPMs have allergen training completed at all times.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

The spray bottle used in the dish area for spraying bleach onto pots and pans bleached out the inspector’s test strips. This indicates a concentration capable of leaving chemical residue on the food contact surfaces. The PIC was shown the strip and remade the solution during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all chemical sanitizers are at safe concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

A container of steak knives is observed soiled with crumbs/debris on the cook line. The PIC was shown and washed both the container as well as the knives during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact utensils are stored so that they are protected from contamination prior to use/service.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A package of styrofoam containers is observed on the floor in the dry storage/ alcohol storage room. The concerns were discussed with the PIC and the items moved during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact items are stored at least 6 inches above the ground at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hand to turn off the faucet prior to acquiring a paper towels to dry their hands. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to. Ensure that all food handlers wash hands safely at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Multiple knives on the magnetic rack in the back of the facility are observed with soiled blades. It is unclear if the items were not completely cleaned or if they were used, partially wiped off and then placed back on the rack. This location should only be for items that are ready for use/cleaned and sanitized. The knives were moved to dish for re-cleaning and the rack sanitized.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 

Two stacks of plates to the left of the prep cooler are observed with food debris/residues between the stacked plates. This indicated that they either had not been completely cleaned or were contaminated prior to ready-for-use storage. The PIC was consulted and moved the stacks of plates to dish for re-cleaning to correct. Ensure that plates are completely cleaned and protected from contamination prior to use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The two sani buckets available for observation in the facility throughout the inspection (bar area and server station) are observed to barely register sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. Both buckets were discussed and remade during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that the sanitizers used in the facility are maintained at effective concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

A fly strip is observed in use hanging from the ceiling above the tortilla storage of the prep line. The PIC was consulted and instructed to place these items in locations that do not pose a concern for contaminating foods or food contact surfaces. They indicated that these strips are normally placed over trash cans, which is acceptable. This particular strip is approximately two feet away from being over a trash can and should be moved. It was removed during this inspection to correct. Ensure that poisonous items are stored so that they do not pose a concern for contamination.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

A park of knives are observed with the blades shoved between a piece of particle board and the wall next to the fountain drink machine in the kitchen. This space is not cleanable and should not have food contact items stored here. Per the PIC these knives are used for lemons slicing during the morning prep work. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the knives moved to dish for cleaning. Ensure that utensils are stored in locations that do not pose a concern for contaminating the food contact sections prior to, or between, uses.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

During this inspection there was not a sani bucket or other method to sanitize surfaces present in the kitchen area of this facility. A bucket was made during this inspection to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use in the food prep areas at all times that foods are being handled.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

The PICs at this facility were unable to provide their employee verification for responsibility to report illness related symptoms and diagnosis. Another copy of the SCDPH reporting agreement was given (in Spanish) during this inspection. The PICs are instructed to ensure that all food handlers sign a copy prior to the follow up in two weeks.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener is observed with heavy accumulation of food debris. PIC was shown the item and instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain the food contact surfaces clean. The blade was cleaned during the inspection to correct the immediate violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Pink slime/mold is observed on the baffle in the ice machine. The PIC was consulted and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving foreword.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Multiple knives on the magnetic rack in the back of the facility are observed with soiled blades. It is unclear if the items were not completely cleaned or if they were used, partially wiped off and then placed back on the rack. This location should only be for items that are ready for use/cleaned and sanitized. The knives were moved to dish for re-cleaning and the rack sanitized.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit.  

Three probes were compared to the inspector’s thermometer and only one showed within an acceptable temperature range. Calibrating the thermometers was discussed and explained during this inspection. New thermometers were opened and put into circulation and the old ones removed until they could be recalibrated.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

A thick accumulation of ice is observed on the floor on the back half of the walk in freezer. The PICs were shown and instructed to remove the ice and clean the area both often enough and sufficiently enough to prevent accumulation in the future.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The metal counter in the back hallway of the kitchen is pulling away from the wall, producing a gap that is not easily cleanable as screws would need to be removed for effective cleaning. Re-seal the counter to the wall prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener is observed with heavy accumulation of food debris. PIC was shown and consulted the item and instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain the food contact surfaces clean. The blade was cleaned during the inspection to correct the immediate violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

The sanitizer in the bar three part sink did not register on the inspector’s test strips. The sink was remade to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

A container of milk is observed in the walk in cooler opened and partially used. PIC indicated that the items were opened yesterday. Date marking was discussed with the PIC and they are aware that the used by date on the container is not an approved date marking system. Date markings were added during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. 

A large pan of ground beef is observed cooling at room temperature. Internal temperatures are observed to range from 118F to 158F depending on were they were taken. Cooling practices we’re discussed. The PIC indicated that the pan was brought off from cooking approximately an hour ago. The pan was allowed to be stirred and move into the walk in cooler for effective cooling. Procedures should ensure that TCS foods are safely/ rapidly cooled through the temperature danger zone.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

A large pan of frozen chicken breasts is observed thawing with standing water. Thawing practices were discussed and the water turned on to correct.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-203.12: (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be accurate to +/- 1.5C. (B) accurate to +/- 3 Fahrenheit.  

Two thermometers are observed in the walk in cooler that are ineffective. One is registering approximately 13 degrees warmer than the air temperature and the other appears to be intended for hot boxes or cooking. A new thermometer was provided during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Multiple flies are observed on the bags of onions in the back shelves of the facility. PIC is instructed to ensure that the flies are removed prior to the follow up in two weeks.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Reporting agreements have only been filled out for less than half of the employees at the facility prior to this inspection. The forms were completed during this inspection to correct the violation at this time. No further follow up will be required at this time.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

During this inspection, neither PIC was able to provide reporting agreements for employees at the facility. findings.comment: REPEAT: No employee reporting agreements on file. CORRECTED-- Inspector provided blank agreement. Have all staff review and sign agreements. Keep on file for review during inspections. Ref. 2-201.11 [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment: REPEAT: No vomit/diarrhea clean up policy on file. CORRECTED-- Inspector provided. Ref. 2-501.11 [Pf]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: PIC does not have access to employee reporting agreements for inspector to review. Ensure that staff are educated on employee health and keep signed reporting agreements on file for review during health inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11 The Person in Charge shall ensure that (O) Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A). [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: PIC does not have access to the vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy must be accessible so it may be referred to in case norovirus clean up is needed.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Employee beverages observed on the top shelves of two vertical coolers (bottled sports/energy drinks) and above the back prep counter (energy drink and an uncovered plastic cup). CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC and employee. Beverages were removed and discarded. Store employee drinks below/away from food and food prep areas so they don't contaminate foods/food prep areas.
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee donned gloves without first washing hands. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Educate staff on when to wash hands, including before putting gloves on.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed employee rinse a spatula in the kitchen handwashing sink. CORRECTED-- Discussed with kitchen staff. Utensils washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the 3 compartment sink. Use handsinks only for handwashing.
Observed bar handwashing sink containing a blender pitcher. CORRECTED-- Pitcher removed from handwashing sink. Handwashing sinks must be maintained accessible at all times and not used for any other purpose than handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Items observed stored in the drawer coolers under the grill as follows: Top drawer- raw beef, chicken and fish; Bottom drawer- sliced bell peppers, cauliflower, and broccoli, chorizo, and raw shrimp. CORRECTED-- Discussed storage order with kitchen staff and re-arranged drawers so that raw animal proteins are stored in the lower drawer.
3-306.13: (A) Raw, unPACKAGED animal FOOD, may not be offered for CONSUMER self-service.  This paragraph does not apply to: (1) CONSUMER self-service of READY-TO-EAT FOODS at buffets or salad bars that serve FOODS such as sushi or raw shellfish; (2) Ready-to-cook individual portions for immediate cooking and consumption on the PREMISES such as CONSUMER-cooked MEATS or CONSUMER-selected ingredients for Mongolian barbecue; or (3) Raw, frozen, shell-on shrimp, or lobster. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: No date marking on two opened gallons of milk (one chocolate, one regular), as well as on multiple items in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Foods will be labeled with the dates they were opened or prepared.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Raw beef observed thawing in one compartment of the prep sink without any thawing technique. CORRECTED-- Beef was still 41F or below. Provided education on thawing methods. Cool running water will be utilized.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Thermometers not observed in the vertical coolers or the prep cooler. Place thermometers inside each cooler where they will be easily readable.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Probe thermometer observed to read 40F at room temperature, and 0F when placed in ice water. Calibrate thermometers to accurately measure temperature. 
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit.  [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Salsas observed in two vertical coolers and walk-in cooler on middle or lower shelves without lids protecting from contamination that may fall from items stored above. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC and staff. Lids added where needed.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: No sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen during inspection. CORRECTED-- Discussed with staff and PIC. Sanitizer bucket was made to correct concentration. Sanitizer bucket must be prepared at all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
PIC does not have access to food handler certificates. Ensure certificates are available for review during health inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
REPEAT #2: PIC has not completed allergen awareness training. Complete ANSI-approved allergen awareness training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]
